form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Blumenthal (for Mr. Markey (for himself and Mr. Blumenthal)) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

form.official-title: To amend title 49, United States Code, to require the Secretary of Transportation to establish a motor vehicle recall assistance program, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Promoting Auto Recalls Toward Safety Act of 2020 or the PARTS Act of 2020.

subsection.text: Subchapter II of chapter 301 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: The term open recall means a motor vehicle recall—

subparagraph.text: for which a notification by a manufacturer has been provided under section 30119; and
that has not been remedied under section 30120.

paragraph.text: The term registration means the process for registering a motor vehicle in a State (including registration renewal).
The term Secretary means the Secretary of Transportation.

Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall establish a program under which the Secretary shall provide grants and other assistance, including technical assistance, to States in informing owners and lessees of a motor vehicle about open recalls on the motor vehicle at the time of registration of the motor vehicle in the State.
To be eligible to receive assistance under this subsection, a State shall—

subparagraph.text: submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require; and

clause.text: to notify each owner or lessee of a motor vehicle presented for registration in the State of any open recall on that motor vehicle; and
to provide to each owner or lessee of the motor vehicle presented for registration—

subclause.text: the open recall information for the motor vehicle at no cost; and
such other information as the Secretary may require.

paragraph.text: In selecting recipients for assistance under this subsection, the Secretary shall take into consideration the methodology of a State for—

subparagraph.text: identifying open recalls on a motor vehicle;
informing the owner or lessee of a motor vehicle of an open recall; and

clause.text: informing owners and lessees about open recalls; and

subparagraph.text: A State may receive not more than 1 grant under this subsection.
A grant provided under this subsection shall require a performance period of 2 years.

paragraph.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of completion of the performance period under paragraph (4)(B), each State that receives a grant under this subsection shall submit to the Secretary a performance report that contains such information as the Secretary considers to be necessary—

subparagraph.text: to evaluate the extent to which open recalls have been remedied in the State; and

clause.text: recall completion under this subsection; and

paragraph.text: Not later than 180 days after the date on which the Secretary receives from a State a performance report under paragraph (5), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.text: evaluate the extent to which open recalls have been remedied in the State; and

submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and make publicly available a report describing the results of the evaluation under subparagraph (A).

subsection.text: The analysis for subchapter II of chapter 301 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by striking the item relating to section 30128 and inserting the following:

toc.toc-entry: 30128. Vehicle rollover prevention and crash mitigation.

subsection.text: Section 30118 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: Each manufacturer that is conducting a campaign under subsection (b) or (c), or any other law (including regulations), to notify manufacturers, distributors, owners, purchasers, or dealers of a defect or noncompliance shall submit to the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration—

subparagraph.text: by the applicable date described in section 573.7(d) of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (or a successor regulation), a quarterly report on the campaign for each of 8 consecutive quarters, beginning with the quarter in which the campaign was initiated; and
an annual report for each of the 3 years following completion of the last quarter for which a quarterly report is submitted under subparagraph (A).

paragraph.text: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, each report under this subsection shall comply with the requirements of section 573.7 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (or a successor regulation).

subsection.header: Scorecard and notification to owners and lessees of unremedied vehicles
subsection.text: Section 30120 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: The Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration shall publish an annual scorecard of recall completion rates for each manufacturer submitting a report under section 30118(f) during the year covered by the scorecard.
The annual scorecard under paragraph (1) shall include—

subparagraph.text: for each manufacturer submitting a report under section 30118(f) during the year covered by the scorecard—

subclause.text: recalls issued by the manufacturer during the year covered by the scorecard; and
vehicles of the manufacturer subject to a recall during the year covered by the scorecard; and

clause.text: the percentage of vehicles of the manufacturer that—

subclause.text: were subject to a recall at any time during the year covered by the scorecard; and
have been remedied under this section; and

subparagraph.text: for each campaign that is the subject of a report submitted under section 30118(f) during the year covered by the scorecard—

clause.text: the total number of recalls issued by the manufacturer pursuant to the campaign—

subclause.text: during the year covered by the scorecard; and
since the date on which the campaign was initiated;

clause.text: the total number of vehicles of the manufacturer subject to the campaign—

subclause.text: during the year covered by the scorecard; and
since the date on which the campaign was initiated; and

clause.text: the percentage of vehicles subject to the campaign that have been remedied under this section—

subclause.text: during the year covered by the scorecard; and
since the date on which the campaign was initiated.
